arxiv-2601-21752.title: Synthesizing Epileptic Seizures: Gaussian Processes for EEG Generation
arxiv-2601-21752.creator: Nina Moutonnet, Joshua Corneck, Felipe Tobar, Danilo Mandic
arxiv-2601-21752.description: Abstract Reliable seizure detection from electroencephalography (EEG) time series is a high-priority clinical goal, yet the acquisition cost and scarcity of labeled EEG data limit the performance of machine learning methods. This challenge is exacerbated by the long-range, high-dimensional, and non-stationary nature of epileptic EEG recordings, which makes realistic data generation particularly difficult.

pmc-11327120.title: Perceived social support and quality of life in endometrial cancer patients: a longitudinal study
pmc-11327120.creator: Vincenzo Dario Mandato, Marcella Paterlini, Federica Torricelli, Elisa Rabitti, Valentina Mastrofilippo, Lorenzo Aguzzoli
pmc-11327120.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess the influence of medical history, perceived physician-patient communication, and perceived social support on changes in the quality of life (QoL) during the first year of follow-up in patients undergoing surgery for endometrial cancer (EC), the most prevalent gynecological cancer in Western countries, especially in Central and Eastern Europe and North America.

pmc-11497676.title: School‐based racial segregation, social support, and late‐life cognitive function in the Study of Healthy Aging in African Americans (STAR)
pmc-11497676.creator: Sirena Gutierrez, Rachel A. Whitmer, Yenee Soh, Rachel Peterson, Kristen M. George, Yi Lor, Lisa L. Barnes, Elizabeth Rose Mayeda, Isabel E. Allen, Jacqueline M. Torres, M. Maria Glymour, Paola Gilsanz
pmc-11497676.description: INTRODUCTIONSchool‐based social support for Black students may mediate or modify the association between school segregation and late‐life cognition.METHODSStudy of Healthy Aging in African Americans participants (n = 574) reported segregated school attendance and school‐based social support. Associations of segregated schooling with domain‐specific cognitive outcomes and effect modification or mediation by school‐based social support were evaluated with linear mixed models.

pmc-11526172.title: Structural basis for human OGG1 processing 8-oxodGuo within nucleosome core particles
pmc-11526172.creator: Mengtian Ren, Fabian Gut, Yilan Fan, Jingke Ma, Xiajing Shan, Aysenur Yikilmazsoy, Mariia Likhodeeva, Karl-Peter Hopfner, Chuanzheng Zhou
pmc-11526172.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Base excision repair (BER) is initialized by DNA glycosylases, which recognize and flip damaged bases out of the DNA duplex into the enzymes active site, followed by cleavage of the glycosidic bond. Recent studies have revealed that all types of DNA glycosylases repair base lesions less efficiently within nucleosomes, and their repair activity is highly depended on the lesion’s location within the nucleosome.

pmc-12595029.title: A large electroencephalogram database of freewill reaching and grasping tasks for brain machine interfaces
pmc-12595029.creator: Bhoj Raj Thapa, John Boggess, Jihye Bae
pmc-12595029.description: Brain machine interfaces (BMIs) offer great potential to improve the quality of life for individuals with neurological disorders or severe motor impairments. Among various neural recording modalities, electroencephalogram (EEG) is particularly favorable for BMIs due to its noninvasive nature, portability, and high temporal resolution.

pmc-13069473.title: Human α2‐Macroglobulin: Architecture, Mechanisms, and Functional Implications
pmc-13069473.creator: Pietro de Carvalho Andrade, Tales Alexandre Costa‐Silva, Gisele Monteiro
pmc-13069473.description: α2‐Macroglobulin (α2M) is a large glycoprotein and one of the most abundant proteins found in the plasma of vertebrates and in the hemolymph of invertebrates. It performs several important functions in the innate immune system, serving as a pan‐protease inhibitor and contributing to essential processes, such as cytokine and hormone transport.

pmc-13183193.title: Research on strategies for enhancing the competency of safety directors in EPC projects empowered by AI
pmc-13183193.creator: Jing Guan, Zhen chao Yang, Congcong Wang
pmc-13183193.description: With the widespread application of the engineering–procurement–construction (EPC) delivery model in large-scale infrastructure and complex industrial projects, the highly dynamic construction environment and the escalating complexity of risks pose heightened requirements for the competency of project safety directors. Conventional approaches that rely primarily on experience and manual inspections have become a bottleneck to further improvements in safety management capability.

pmc-13232527.title: Genetic dissection of protein content in cowpea using custom-made NIRS equations and GWAS as a model for nutritional breeding and undergraduate research training
pmc-13232527.creator: Habib Akinmade, Shiri Ben-Israel, Audrey Ryan, Chase Johnson, Annmary Tharayil, Rebecca Olivia Arias, Rebecca Caroline Ulbricht Ferreira, Claudio Fernandes, Ziynet Boz, Esteban Rios, T Jamann
pmc-13232527.description: As the demand for plant-based nutrition increases, improving the protein profile of legumes like cowpea has become a breeding priority. Cowpea, a multiuse legume and staple in many low-income regions, provides important dietary protein that can help meet the demand in our growing population.

pmc-13280544.title: Advances in neuroimaging studies of thalamic abnormalities in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
pmc-13280544.creator: Jiaqi Zhou, Ruilin Jin, Teng Zhu, Jiayun Yu, Xiaolei Cen, Qiqiong Feng, Yinan Mo, Mengjie Zhang, Wanying Zheng, Yanchi Wang, Rui Huang, Hanlin Li, Chuang Yang
pmc-13280544.description: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder whose core pathological mechanism is deeply rooted in the dysfunction of the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuit. This review summarizes recent advances in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies investigating thalamic abnormalities in children with ADHD, highlighting multidimensional pathological changes within the thalamus.

pmc-13671232.title: Mapping the frontiers of genomic disease surveillance research in the ASEAN region: scientometric insights for precision public health and next-generation epidemic intelligence
pmc-13671232.creator: Jerico Bautista Ogaya, Rahmatullah Nazari, Olalekan John Okesanya, Andres Phillip Mayol, Emmanueal M Cabanig, Mohamed Mustaf Ahmed, Murtaza Jafari, Roel Nickelson M Solano, Joey Salinas Ramos, Zhinya Kawa Othman, Adriana Viola Miranda, Shuaibu Saidu Musa, Mae Frances G Sanico, Rolando A Alimen, Lin
pmc-13671232.description: Genomic disease surveillance has become a cornerstone of precision public health, yet the regional research architecture in Southeast Asia remains insufficiently characterized. This study provides a comprehensive scientometric mapping of genomic surveillance research in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) region and identifies patterns relevant to the development of epidemic intelligence systems.

uslaw-usc-t50-s3979.title: 50 U.S.C. § 3979 — Review of findings of fact and conclusions of law
uslaw-usc-t50-s3979.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t50-s3979.description: United States Code, Title 50 (War And National Defense); Chapter 50 (Servicemembers Civil Relief); Subchapter IV (Life Insurance). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The findings of fact and conclusions of law made by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in administering this subchapter are subject to review on appeal to the Board of Veterans’ Appeals pursuant to chapter 71 of title 38 and.
